| rf_ask_plain | Links on one data page, and the known addresses of the agency's data service, its terms of use, its change log and its data inventory. |
| rf_fail | At least one object the agency is shown to publish (named in the result) is neither linked from this data page nor at a standard address the check looked at — the inventory at /data.json on the data page's own host (an inventory on the main www site while the page sits on a subdomain is not matched there), or the API catalog at /.well-known/api-catalog. For the service's terms and the changelog no published standard exists, so a fail on either rests only on this project's "must be linked" rule and breaks no published convention. It is not a claim that the object is missing, nor that a client told where to look cannot use it. |
| rf_hypothesis | Can a machine client that starts at a data page, and knows nothing else, reach the four objects an agency publishes for machines (its API, the API's terms, its changelog, its data inventory)? An SI client usually arrives at a data page from a search result; if the objects behind it cannot be reached from there, the client cannot use them, however well they are built. |
| rf_name_brief | From a data page to the data service, terms, change log and inventory |
| rf_not_measured | The public client could not settle one or more objects, for one of three reasons: the host refused the identified client; the client's own robots.txt compliance kept it from reading; or it could not confirm an absence, or a server or network error stopped it — here, an object whose existence was not settled, a page not served or its links not read, or an API catalog address no collector has fetched yet. |
| rf_partial | Some of the agency's data pages that were looked at reached every published object and some did not. |
| rf_pass | Every object the agency is shown to publish is either linked from this data page or sits at its published standard address. |
| rf_plain_name | Page reaches the agency's API, terms, changelog, inventory |
| rf_question | Starting at one of the agency's data pages and knowing nothing else, can a machine client reach the four things an agency publishes for machines — its data service (its API), that service's terms, its changelog, and its data inventory? |
| rf_requirements | [{"source": "rfc-9727-api-catalog", "quote": "SHALL resolve an HTTPS GET request to /.well-known/api-catalog and return an API catalog document"}, {"source": "rfc-9727-api-catalog", "quote": "This identifies a target resource that represents a list of APIs available from the Publisher of the link context."}, {"source": "m-25-05-phase-2-implementation-of-the-evidence-act-open-gove", "quote": "each agency must post the inventory in JSON format, or a successor format, to www.[agency].gov/data.json"}, {"source": "rfc-9727-api-catalog", "quote": "the Publisher \"example\" could include the api-catalog link relation in the HTTP header and/or content payload"}] |
| rf_rung_two_changes | Nothing: this check needs no key. |
| rf_state | project_defined |
| rf_tells_plain | Whether a program that starts on a data page can find everything the agency offers for machines. |
| rf_what_client_does | The public client makes no new request of its own; it reuses what other checks already fetched: the data page's links and headers, and whether each object was served where it was recorded. |
| rf_where_we_look | At one of the agency's data pages — its links and its response headers — and at the recorded locations where each of the four objects was reported to sit. |
| rf_who_else | No public tool runs this exact check. |
| rf_why_it_matters | An RFC on API catalogs defines how a publisher announces its data service at a standard address, and an OMB memo requires each agency to post its data inventory at a set data.json address. Reaching the service's terms or changelog by an ordinary link, and combining the four objects into one result, are the project's own rules. |
| rf_why_short | A web standard sets an address for listing data services, and an OMB memo fixes where the inventory lives; joining the four is this project's rule. |
| rule_id | RULE-A13-v1 |
| signal | Per surface, per object (the API, its terms, its changelog, the inventory): pass when an object that exists (an Observation at a recorded location served it, or the record says verified) has a recorded URL among the product page's links, on-host or off-host and past the link probe's cap, or sits at a convention location (the well-known api-catalog URI served as a Linkset, or a `Link: rel="api-catalog"` header, RFC 9727; the data.json inventory at the host root, OMB M-13-13); fail when it exists, the page was read whole and neither holds; error when existence is not settled, the page was not read, or the API's convention location was not fetched; not_applicable when no object is shown to exist. The surface's verdict is the first of fail, error, pass, not_applicable that any object returns. |

## Other record fields

| field | value |
|---|---|
| candidate_rationale | DN-013-R1: existence is not discoverability. The harness tested whether a stranger could find an agency's API, inventory, terms or changelog from the product page and reported the failure of that search as the absence of the thing, while api.census.gov, api.bls.gov, api.eia.gov and the BEA API are public knowledge. The existence legs (A2, D1, F4, D4 and D4's consumers) now read recorded and seeded locations only; what the link probe and the guessed paths measured is this indicator: a machine that knows only the product page, and the conventions, gets there or it does not. |
